written: 2026-09-20, before any pipeline run on this book; chapter numbers checked against pg1400.txt
note: chapter = the chapter in which the reader first learns the fact. Before that chapter starts, no card, relation, event, biography or recap may state it; two chapters later it should be visible.

probes.claim: Mrs. Joe Gargery (Pip's sister) has died.
probes.source: Ch. XXXIV: letter says Mrs. J. Gargery had departed this life on Monday last

probes.claim: Compeyson has died (drowned in the river).
probes.source: Ch. LIV: struggle in the river during the escape; Ch. LV: Compeyson was tumbling on the tides, dead

probes.claim: Magwitch (the convict, also called Provis) has died.
probes.source: Ch. LVI: he dies in the prison infirmary
Ch. LVII: 'Is she dead, Joe?' — Joe confirms
Ch. LIX: death of her husband from an accident with a horse

probes.claim: Estella is going to marry, or has married, Bentley Drummle.
probes.source: Ch. XLIV: 'I am going to be married to him.'

probes.claim: Joe and Biddy are married (Biddy is Joe's wife).
probes.source: Ch. LVIII: 'It's my wedding-day, and I am married to Joe!'

probes.claim: The convict (Magwitch/Provis) is Pip's secret benefactor, the source of Pip's fortune or great expectations.
probes.source: Ch. XXXIX: the convict returns and reveals he made Pip a gentleman

probes.claim: Magwitch (Provis, the convict) is Estella's father.
probes.source: Ch. L: Herbert relays Provis's story of his lost child; Pip realises Provis is Estella's father

probes.claim: Molly, Mr. Jaggers's housekeeper, is Estella's mother.
probes.source: Ch. XLVIII: 'I felt absolutely certain that this woman was Estella's mother.'

probes.claim: Compeyson is the man who courted and jilted Miss Havisham (her false lover).
probes.source: Ch. XLII: Herbert's note — Compeyson is the man who professed to be Miss Havisham's lover

probes.claim: Orlick is the one who attacked Mrs. Joe (struck her down).
probes.source: Ch. LIII: 'It was you as did for your shrew sister.' — Orlick admits it was he

probes.claim: The pale young gentleman Pip fought is Herbert Pocket.
probes.source: Ch. XXI: 'And you are the pale young gentleman!'

probes.claim: Miss Havisham's dress caught fire and she was badly burned.
probes.source: Ch. XLIX: her dress catches fire from the grate
